edition.locus: Gebhardt II.21-29a (threats; Carpus racked silent; Papylus the citizen)

source_text: Ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Πολλὰ ἐάσας σε φλυαρῆσαι εἰς βλασφημίαν ἤγαγόν σε τῶν θεῶν καὶ τῶν Σεβαστῶν· ἵνα οὖν μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σοι προχωρήσῃ, θύεις; Ἢ τί λέγεις; Κάρπος εἶπεν· Ἀδύνατον ὅτι θύω, οὐ γὰρ πώποτε ἔθυσα εἰδώλοις. Εὐθὺς οὖν ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν κρεμασθέντα ξέεσθαι. Ὁ δὲ ἔλεγεν· Χριστιανός εἰμι. Ἐπὶ πολὺ δὲ βοώμενος ἔκαμνεν καὶ οὐκέτι ἴσχυσεν λαλῆσαι. Καὶ ἐάσας τὸν Κάρπον ὁ ἀνθύπατος ἐπὶ τὸν Παπύλον ἐτρέπετο, λέγων αὐτῷ· Βουλευτής εἶ; Ὁ δὲ λέγων· Πολίτης εἰμί. Ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Τίνων πολίτης; Παπύλος εἶπεν· Θυατείρων. Ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Τέκνα ἔχεις;
pass_a_gloss: The proconsul said: after permitting you to babble many things I brought you into blasphemy of the gods and of the Augusti; in order therefore that it not advance further for you, do you sacrifice, or what do you say; Carpus said: it is impossible that I sacrifice, for never did I sacrifice to idols; immediately therefore he ordered him, after being hung up, to be scraped; and he kept saying: I am a Christian; and after crying out for a long time he grew weary and no longer had strength to speak; and leaving Carpus the proconsul turned to Papylus, saying to him: are you a councillor; and he said: I am a citizen; the proconsul said: citizen of whom; Papylus said: of the Thyatirans; the proconsul said: do you have children.
pass_b_english: The proconsul said, “I have let you chatter on at length, and led you into reviling the gods and the Augusti. So, lest you go still further, will you sacrifice? What do you say?” Carpus said, “I cannot sacrifice, for I have never sacrificed to idols.” At once, therefore, he ordered him to be hung up and scraped. But he kept saying, “I am a Christian.” After crying out for a long time, he grew exhausted and was no longer able to speak.

Then the proconsul left Carpus aside and turned to Papylus, saying to him, “Are you a councillor?” And he replied, “I am a citizen.” The proconsul said, “A citizen of what people?” Papylus said, “Of Thyatira.” The proconsul asked him whether he had children.

choices.english: after letting you chatter on at length
choices.why: aorist participle ἐάσας gives prior permission and πολλὰ with infinitive gives extent, so rendered as concession of lengthy speech
ἀδύνατον with ὅτι plus present indicative expresses impossibility of the act for the speaker in this context, not abstract possibility
rejected: it is impossible that I may sacrifice

choices.english: after crying out for a long time he grew exhausted
choices.why: ἐπὶ πολὺ marks duration and the present participle βοώμενος with imperfect ἔκαμνεν shows prolonged crying leading to exhaustion
